facts_zh:
Dozens of gold prospectors killed in strikes on Egypt-Sudan border, rights group says
- Published
At least 72 civilians who had been prospecting for gold in a border region of Sudan have been killed in air strikes, a regional rights group says.
Emergency Lawyers, based in the Sudanese capital, Khartoum, said jets targeted the so-called artisanal miners at a popular gold mining sites in Sudan's River Nile state on Saturday.
Neither the Egyptian government nor the de facto Sudanese authorities have so far commented.

Orangutans released back into Borneo forest after devastating fires
- Published
Eight orangutans have been released back into the wild in Borneo after they were taken into captivity when their habitat was threatened by wildfires over the summer.
Three mothers, their three daughters and two adult males were freed in a reserve in the west of the island on Friday, International Animal Rescue Indonesia (Yiari) and the forestry ministry said.
Indonesian authorities rescued 46 orangutans from fires in August and September.

facts_zh:
Children among 139 dead after boat capsizes off Djibouti, UN says
- Published
At least 139 migrants including 15 children have died and dozens more are still missing after a boat sank off the coast of Djibouti, the UN's migration office has said.
The boat had been travelling from Djibouti to Yemen with 305 people aboard when it capsized near the port town of Obock on Thursday night.
Around 82 people were rescued, the International Organization for Migration (IOM) said.

Ukraine strikes Yandex data centre in third attack on Russian tech giant
- Published
Yandex has been forced to pause its operations at a data centre near Moscow after the facility was damaged in a Ukrainian drone strike - the third attack on the Russian tech giant's sites this week.
The company - dubbed "Russia's Google" - said no one was injured at the centre in Vladimir, east of the capital, but some of its services were unavailable to users.
Earlier this week, Yandex said it was struggling to maintain its services after two of its five data centres were hit in Ukrainian strikes.

articles.title_zh: Pope Leo to have surgery after lump found on lung
facts_zh:
Pope Leo to have surgery after lump found on lung
- Published
Pope Leo XIV has announced he will be operated on "in the coming days" after a nodule was found on his lung during a medical check-up.
"The doctors found an early, well-localised nodule on my lung," he told the public during his weekly Sunday prayers in St Peter's Square in Rome.

The 71-year-old said his medical team "believe it would be right to intervene" and he had agreed to the operation, while reassuring pilgrims that the mass was "well-contained" and caught "at an early stage".

all_titles.en: Pope Leo to have surgery after lump found on lung

articles.title_original: US justice department investigates TV networks over Trump pool coverage
articles.title_zh: US justice department investigates TV networks over Trump pool coverage
facts_zh:
US justice department investigates TV networks over Trump pool coverage
- Published
The US justice department (DoJ) has said it is investigating several TV networks over whether they broke federal competition laws when they recently suspended pool coverage of President Donald Trump.
Last month, five networks paused their presidential coverage for several days in response to the Trump administration withdrawing the credentials of reporters from CNN, MS Now and Politico.

The justice department asked ABC, CBS, CNN, NBC and Fox News to hand over communications related to the pool and said that the boycott could violate the Sherman Act, referring to a law that bars companies from engaging in monopolistic business practices.

all_titles.en: US justice department investigates TV networks over Trump pool coverage
